fields.Participants: VP Store Operations, CMO, CFO, Category Manager

workflows.name: Contractor Loyalty Program Tier Design & Benefit Structure Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews contractor loyalty tier structure" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "discount by tier" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approves program financial model" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-371 (ensure controlled execution — Contractor Loyalty, Incentive & Volume Program (PA-43.2).)
- operational: VP Store Operations review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tier compression**: If tier thresholds are too low, most accounts qualify for Silver/Gold, diluting the exclusivity that drives aspirational spending
- **Benefit cost escalation**: Generous benefits (e.g., 15% Platinum discount) may erode margin below acceptable levels on high-volume accounts; ensure minimum margin floor per category
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by VP Store Operations, CMO, CFO, and IT
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty tier management module with auto-classification (W1886.4a)
- Benefit activation per tier in POS, CRM, and ecommerce (W1886.4b)
- Financial modeling for program ROI (W1886.3)
- Integration with W1549 (contractor annual spend tier review), W17 (consumer loyalty — separate program), W104 (loyalty financial governance)

steps.activity: Annual: VP Store Operations reviews contractor loyalty tier structure: (a) current tiers per the W1549 register: Bronze (PHP 100K–500K/year), Silver (PHP 500K–1.5M), Gold (PHP 1.5M–5M), Platinum (PHP 5M+), (b) evaluate tier distribution: are too many accounts in Bronze (devaluing program) or too few in Platinum (unattainable)?, (c) competitive benchmarking: what do CitiHardware, Wilcon Depot, and ACE Hardware offer trade professionals?, (d) member satisfaction survey: do contractors value current benefits? What benefits would increase loyalty?

VP Store Operations and CMO redesign benefit structure: (a) pricing benefits: trade discount by tier (Bronze 5%, Silver 8%, Gold 12%, Platinum 15%), (b) service benefits: priority delivery scheduling, dedicated phone line, extended store hours access, (c) credit benefits: higher credit limits, longer payment terms for higher tiers, (d) experiential benefits: exclusive contractor events, product training, jobsite visits by Category Managers, (e) partner benefits: discounts from partner businesses (insurance, fuel, vehicle rental), (f) financial modeling: cost of benefits per tier vs. incremental margin from higher spend

CFO approves program financial model: (a) total program cost (discounts, benefits, points liability) vs. incremental revenue from tier-based spend uplift, (b) target ROI: program cost should not exceed 2–3% of B2B revenue, (c) points liability impact on balance sheet per W1893

IT configures loyalty tier rules in POS and CRM: (a) tier thresholds and auto-upgrade/downgrade rules, (b) benefit activation per tier, (c) points earning rates per tier (higher tiers earn points faster), (d) test configuration before go-live

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Cashier, Trade Professional, Loyalty System
fields.Trigger: Contractor purchase at POS; points redemption request
fields.Volume: ~5,200 trade accounts earning and redeeming points

workflows.name: Contractor Points Earning, Redemption & Statement Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Contractor makes purchase at POS using trade account card" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-capture of "enters redemption amount" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "preview" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-371 (ensure controlled execution — Contractor Loyalty, Incentive & Volume Program (PA-43.2).)
- operational: Account Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Points liability growth**: Unredeemed points accumulate as a liability on the balance sheet; if redemption rate is low, liability grows unchecked; encourage redemption through targeted promotions
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — automated system with AM oversight
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty points engine integrated with POS and trade account system (W1887.1)
- Points earning rate configuration per tier (W1887.1b)
- Redemption processing at POS and online (W1887.2)
- Monthly statement generation and distribution (W1887.3)
- Integration with W17 (consumer loyalty — same engine, different program), W5B (POS selling), W10.1 (ecommerce platform)

steps.activity: Contractor makes purchase at POS using trade account card: (a) system identifies trade account and loyalty tier, (b) points earned per spend: Bronze 1 point per PHP 100, Silver 1.5 per PHP 100, Gold 2 per PHP 100, Platinum 3 per PHP 100, (c) system posts points to contractor's loyalty account with transaction reference, (d) points visible in contractor's online portal and mobile app

Contractor redeems points: (a) at POS: contractor presents trade account card and requests points redemption; cashier enters redemption amount; system converts points to peso value (1 point = PHP 1.00), (b) online: contractor redeems points for merchandise or gift items through trade portal, (c) points deduction posted to loyalty account; redemption value reduces transaction total or issued as store credit

Monthly: system generates contractor loyalty statement: (a) points earned this month and year-to-date, (b) points redeemed this month and year-to-date, (c) current points balance and peso equivalent, (d) current tier and progress to next tier, (e) next tier benefits preview, (f) statement sent via email and available in trade portal

Quarterly: Account Manager reviews points liability for assigned accounts: (a) total unredeemed points per account, (b) accounts with high points balances that may indicate dissatisfaction (earning but not redeeming = not engaging with program benefits), (c) accounts approaching tier upgrade — proactive communication to encourage next-tier spend

fields.Frequency: Quarterly calculation for Gold/Platinum; annual for Bronze/Silver
fields.Participants: FP&A, Account Manager, Finance, Trade Professional
fields.Trigger: Annual/quarterly volume rebate calculation period end
fields.Volume: ~200 Gold/Platinum accounts eligible for volume rebates

workflows.name: Contractor Volume Rebate & Spend-Based Incentive Calculation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "FP&A calculates volume rebate per eligible account" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-communication of "communicates rebate to trade professional" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-update of "update trade account balance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-371 (ensure controlled execution — Contractor Loyalty, Incentive & Volume Program (PA-43.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin erosion**: Cumulative effect of trade discount (5–15%) + loyalty points (1–3%) + volume rebate (1–2.5%) can reduce effective margin below acceptable levels; FP&A must monitor total trade program cost per account
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by FP&A and Account Managers
System Touchpoints: - Volume rebate calculation engine with configurable tier rates (W1888.1)
- Rebate credit memo generation linked to AR (W1888.3a)
- Integration with W39 (vendor rebate — similar logic, vendor side), W85 (product costing — margin impact)

steps.activity: FP&A calculates volume rebate per eligible account: (a) total qualifying spend during period (exclude returns, taxes, non-merchandise), (b) apply rebate rate per the W1161/W1549 spend tiers: (i) Bronze PHP 100K–500K: 1% rebate, (ii) Silver PHP 500K–1.5M: 1.5%, (iii) Gold PHP 1.5M–5M: 2%, (iv) Platinum PHP 5M+: 2.5%, (c) rebate paid as credit memo to trade account (applied against future purchases) or as direct refund

Account Manager communicates rebate to trade professional: (a) present rebate calculation with supporting spend data, (b) explain how rebate will be applied (credit memo or refund), (c) encourage reinvestment: suggest using rebate credit for upcoming project materials
Finance processes rebate: (a) credit memo: Dr. Trade Promotion Expense / Cr. Accounts Receivable — Trade Account, (b) refund: Dr. Trade Promotion Expense / Cr. Cash, (c) update trade account balance

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Referred Contractor, Existing Contractor, Marketing
fields.Trigger: Existing trade account refers a new contractor to BuildRight

workflows.name: Contractor Referral Program & New Account Acquisition Incentive

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "logged in CRM with referrer account number" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Account Manager contacts referred contractor" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracks referral conversion rate" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fraud risk**: Contractors may create fake referrals to earn bonus points; validate new accounts are genuine businesses before awarding referral bonus; mitigated by standard operating procedures and system-enforced validation rules
System Touchpoints: - Referral tracking in CRM (W1889.1b)
- Automated referral bonus points posting (W1889.3a)
- Referral conversion analytics (W1889.3c)

steps.activity: Existing trade account refers new contractor: (a) provides new contractor's name, contact, and trade type, (b) referral logged in CRM with referrer account number

Account Manager contacts referred contractor: (a) introduce BuildRight trade program, (b) offer referral incentive: 500 loyalty points for the referring contractor upon new account activation, (c) process new account application per W1878
Upon new account activation: (a) system awards referral bonus points to referring contractor, (b) new contractor receives welcome bonus: 200 loyalty points, (c) AM tracks referral conversion rate

fields.Participants: Finance, Account Manager, Trade Professional, Bank
fields.Trigger: Trade account elects early payment on eligible invoices
fields.Volume: Available to Gold and Platinum tier accounts

workflows.name: Contractor Early Payment Discount & Supply Chain Finance Program

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Finance offers early payment incentive to Gold/Platinum trade accounts" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-collect of "collection reduces working capital needs" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin impact**: 2% discount on top of existing trade discounts and volume rebates may push total program cost above acceptable levels; monitor total trade program cost per account
System Touchpoints: - Early payment discount configuration in AR module (W1890.1)
- Discount application at payment receipt (W1890.2)
- Program cost/benefit analytics (W1890.3)
- Integration with W8 (AR processing), W30 (treasury), W324 (supply chain finance)

steps.activity: Finance offers early payment incentive to Gold/Platinum trade accounts: (a) 2/10 Net 30: 2% discount if paid within 10 days instead of standard Net 30, (b) BuildRight benefits from improved cash flow from trade accounts (receivables collected faster), (c) trade account benefits from cost savings on materials

Trade account elects early payment: (a) pays invoice within discount window, (b) Finance processes payment with 2% discount applied, (c) Dr. Cash (98%) / Dr. Sales Discount (2%) / Cr. Accounts Receivable (100%)

Quarterly: Finance evaluates early payment program cost vs. benefit: (a) total discount cost (2% of accelerated receivables), (b) cash flow benefit (earlier collection reduces working capital needs), (c) annualized cost of discount vs. cost of borrowing — if discount cost < borrowing cost, program is financially beneficial

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, CMO, Category Manager, Account Manager

workflows.name: Contractor Seasonal Promotion & Project Bundle Pricing Execution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "discount for contractors" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-post of "Post-promotion analysis" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-371 (ensure controlled execution — Contractor Loyalty, Incentive & Volume Program (PA-43.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cannibalization**: Trade promotions may cannibalize regular trade pricing (contractors stockpile during promotions rather than buying at regular price); limit purchase quantities during promotional periods
System Touchpoints: - Promotional pricing configuration in POS and ecommerce per W14 (marketing campaign)
- Trade-only pricing rules enforced by account type at POS
- Promotion analytics with trade account participation tracking
- Integration with W14 (marketing campaigns), W40 (price management), W57 (promotional stock)

steps.activity: Category Manager proposes trade-specific promotions: (a) summer construction season (Mar–May): cement and rebar bundle discount for contractors, (b) back-to-school build (May–Jun): paint and electrical bundle for school renovation projects, (c) Q4 project closeout (Oct–Dec): appliance and fixture packages for turnover-ready units, (d) each promotion includes: eligible products, trade-only pricing, minimum quantity, promotional period, margin impact

CMO executes trade promotion communication: (a) direct email/SMS to trade accounts with personalized pricing based on tier, (b) trade portal banner and featured products, (c) AM outreach to key and growth accounts with personalized offer, (d) in-store signage at contractor-frequented departments

Post-promotion analysis: (a) Category Manager and FP&A evaluate: incremental sales volume, margin impact, trade account participation rate, inventory sell-through, (b) adjust future promotions based on performance

fields.Frequency: Monthly dashboard; annual comprehensive ROI analysis
fields.Trigger: Monthly and annual program performance review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "discount cost" (replaces manual Step 1).
Controls: - CTL-371 (ensure controlled execution — Contractor Loyalty, Incentive & Volume Program (PA-43.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Attribution difficulty**: Separating program-driven revenue growth from organic growth is challenging; use cohort analysis (program members vs. similar non-member trade accounts) for attribution
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by FP&A
System Touchpoints: - Trade program cost analytics with multi-dimensional breakdown (W1892.1)
- ROI calculation model with pre-program baseline comparison (W1892.2)
- Integration with W85 (product costing & margin), W35 (financial reporting), W67 (store performance)

steps.activity: Monthly: FP&A compiles trade program cost dashboard: (a) trade discount cost: total discount amount as % of B2B revenue, (b) volume rebate accrual: total rebates earned/accrued, (c) loyalty points cost: points issued valued at PHP 1/point, (d) early payment discount cost, (e) promotional pricing cost, (f) referral bonus cost, (g) AM compensation allocation to trade program, (h) total program cost as % of B2B revenue, (i) trend: is program cost increasing or decreasing?

Annual: FP&A conducts comprehensive ROI analysis: (a) total program cost vs. B2B revenue growth, (b) B2B revenue growth rate vs. pre-program baseline, (c) B2B gross margin with program vs. estimated margin without program, (d) trade account retention rate vs. target, (e) new account acquisition rate and lifetime value, (f) program ROI: (incremental gross margin − program cost) ÷ program cost, (g) recommend program adjustments: benefit reductions if ROI < 150%; benefit enhancements if ROI > 300%
CFO presents annual program ROI to CEO and Board: (a) program financial performance, (b) competitive positioning, (c) recommended adjustments for next year

fields.Participants: Finance, VP Store Operations, External Auditor
fields.Trigger: Monthly financial close; annual loyalty liability review

workflows.name: Contractor Loyalty Program Financial Governance & Liability Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "posts loyalty points liability" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "reviews loyalty liability adequacy" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "methodology" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-371 (ensure controlled execution — Contractor Loyalty, Incentive & Volume Program (PA-43.2).)
- operational: Finance review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Liability overstatement/understatement**: If breakage estimate is wrong, loyalty liability is misstated on the balance sheet; regular calibration with actual redemption data is essential
Staffing Implication: - No incremental headcount — absorbed by Finance
System Touchpoints: - Loyalty points liability module with automated monthly posting (W1893.1)
- Breakage estimation engine (W1893.1c)
- Liability adequacy review analytics (W1893.2)
- Integration with W104 (loyalty financial governance — consumer program), W9A (month-end close), W9B (year-end close)

steps.activity: Monthly: Finance posts loyalty points liability: (a) Dr. Loyalty Program Expense / Cr. Deferred Revenue — Loyalty Points (for points issued during the month valued at redemption rate), (b) upon redemption: Dr. Deferred Revenue — Loyalty Points / Cr. Revenue (or contra-revenue), (c) estimate breakage: % of points that will never be redeemed based on historical pattern (typically 15–25% for trade programs)

Quarterly: Finance reviews loyalty liability adequacy: (a) total liability balance vs. redemption trend, (b) is breakage estimate still appropriate? Adjust if actual redemption patterns change, (c) liability as % of B2B revenue — flag if > 3% (program cost growing faster than revenue)
Annual: External Auditor tests loyalty liability: (a) verify liability calculation methodology, (b) test breakage assumption against historical data, (c) assess completeness of points outstanding
